page.layout: One page of text in a single column. Running head at top left ("LIBER IIII."), page number at top right (297). No marginal notes. Signature at bottom right ("T 5"). A decorative ornament in the left margin is not text.

main_text.l: torum impetus nauis iactatione efficiat, me-
dióque interposito, Aestus maris: facilè
concludetur, quod medio adhærescit, ei quoque
cui medium conuenit, necessariò conuenire.
CAP. IIII.
VOT funt Medij collocandi formæ?
Tres. Nam aut inter duos quæstionis
terminos interponitur, qui locus
Medio maximè conuenit: aut supra
utrunque, aut sub utroque. unde tres Syllogi-
smi figuræ ab Aristotele factæ sunt: prima ex lo-
co Medij dignisimo: secunda ex eo qui mi-
nus dignus est: tertia ex infimo.
Quomodo medium inter utrunque extre-
mum interiicitur? Cum primo loco maius
extremum de ipso dicitur: pòst ipsum de mi-
nore. Nam propositio fit ex medio & attribu-
to: assumptio ex subiecto & medio. unde subiecti
& attributi cōuenientia perspicitur. Sci-
tum est autem, quod Aristoteles scribit, ex fi-
guris omnibus hanc esse ad docendum acco-
mmodatissimā, & mathematicas omnes scien-
tias, veluti Arithmeticā, & Geometriam, suas
in hac figura demōstrationes concludere: pro-
pterea quòd omnes quæ caussa rei fit, decla-
rant. certissimum autem & exquisitissimū sci-
endi genus esse, per quod rei cuiusque caussa
intelligitur.

page.notes: Printing errors left as printed: "dignisimo" (for dignissimo), "caussa" as printed with double long s. The word "sci-endi" at the line break is doubtful, read as "sciendi" with the hyphen at the break. The opening word of the chapter is set in small capitals ("VOT"); the initial letter is uncertain and may be Q ("Quot"), so it is copied as printed. The "&" forms are ligatures and are copied as "&" where they appear as the Latin ampersand. The "ct" ligature in "iactatione" is read as printed.
